findings.summary: Both crash implementations prohibit cancellation of committed outcomes at every deadline. Stalls freeze admission and preserve the original draw; the former selective-refund attack now reverts for all tested roles and deadlines.
Superseded by unconditional non-cancellation: neither missing nor verified entropy permits a LIVE refund, including gas-starved calls.
An overdue keeper now attempts the original relay before settlement and recovery instead of skipping relay after the long timeout.

Original-result-only recovery eliminates cancellation bias but requires eventual publication and delivery of the committed beacon result. Permanent nonpublication leaves unsettled stakes pending. Independent review of this custody/availability boundary and production incident evidence remain required.
An overdue observation is discarded instead of being labelled fresh. The buyback remains disabled until a new complete bounded window is observed.
The burn engine rejects an integer minimum output of zero before any swap or ETH transfer.
Full-width observation timestamps and uint32 interval configuration bounds prevent a whole accumulator timestamp epoch from masquerading as a short fresh interval.
